title: Note text: keep Draft text while Editing, save it when Editing ends
lede: Typing in a Note used to call `setText` on the Notes store on every key, so every keystroke re-ran the Local copy's save timer. Now typing changes only the **Draft text**, held in the Editing module (`src/ui/editing.ts`) next to `editingId`. Editing's single exit, `end`, clears it, and the Notes store, which follows the UI store, **saves it to the Note once**, however Editing ended: a press anywhere else, Escape, focus arriving on another Note, a new Note, a delete, or the page being hidden.

files.question: Where does the Draft text live, and what hands it over?
files.summary: `draftText` sits in the Editing state; `typed` sets it, `end` clears it, and `endedDraft(before, after)` says which text a transition ended Editing with.
files.owns: The Draft text, and the rule that every way Editing ends hands it over (including the new `pageHidden`).
files.never: Touches the Notes store: it only reports what Editing ended with.
files.tested: `src/notes/notesActions.test.ts`, describe `Draft text`: every ending saves it, nothing typed saves nothing, typing while not Editing is dropped.

files.question: How do callers report typing and the page being hidden?
files.summary: Two new actions, `typed` and `pageHidden`, each one `set` of an Editing transition.
files.never: Needs the Notes store: it still doesn't import it.
files.tested: Through the Notes store tests above and the browser tests.

files.question: Who saves the Draft text, and when does Undo see it?
files.summary: A `ui.subscribe` callback saves the ended Draft text with `setText`; `deleteNote` reads the Note for Undo only after reporting `deleted(id)`.
files.owns: Writing the Draft text into the Note, synchronously, before the action that ended Editing carries on.
files.never: Runs on a keystroke: typing doesn't change the UI store's `editingId`, so `endedDraft` returns `null`.
files.tested: `notesActions.test.ts`: one store update per Editing, and delete then Undo brings the typed text back.

files.question: Which component re-renders while typing?
files.summary: While Editing, the textarea is `NoteEditor`, the only subscriber to `draftText`; it shows the Note's saved text until something is typed.
files.owns: Reporting each change as `typed`, and caret and focus as before.
files.tested: `editing.browser.test.tsx`, describe `Draft text`, in Chromium and Firefox.

files.question: What happens to the Draft text when the tab closes?
files.summary: On `pagehide`, Editing ends first, which saves the Draft text, and then the Local copy's scheduled write is flushed.
files.owns: The order of those two calls.
files.never: Runs in tests: `renderApp` leaves the Local copy out.
files.tested: Only the store side (`pageHidden` saves the Draft text) is unit-tested; the listener itself isn't, see notes.

steps.title: input in Note a's textarea
steps.explain: The textarea is `NoteEditor`, mounted only while a is in Editing. Each change is reported as `typed`; nothing calls the Notes store.

steps.title: The Editing module keeps it as Draft text
steps.explain: Only while a Note is in Editing; the same text twice keeps the state reference, so nobody is notified.

steps.title: Only NoteEditor re-renders
steps.explain: `draftText` is selected by `NoteEditor` alone, so other Notes, the Board and the toolbar don't re-render. The UI store's subscribers run, including the Notes store's, but `endedDraft` sees `editingId` unchanged and returns `null`: the browser test counts zero Notes store updates while typing.

steps.title: keydown Escape: Editing ends through the single exit
steps.explain: `end` returns `NOT_EDITING` plus the reason, so the Draft text is cleared in the same transition that ends Editing.

steps.title: The Notes store saves the ended Draft text, once
steps.explain: Zustand calls subscribers synchronously inside `set`, with the state before and after. `before` had a's id and its Draft text; `after` has none, so `setText` runs once. Exactly one Notes store update, which the Local copy saves 300 ms later.

scenarios.name: Delete the Note being edited, then Undo

steps.title: click on Note a's × with Draft text typed
steps.explain: `deleted(id)` ends Editing first. Its `set` runs the subscriber, which saves the Draft text into a. Only then is a read for the Undo snapshot, so the snapshot has the typed text. Reading it before `deleted`, as the code did before this PR, would make Undo bring back the old text.

steps.title: Undo
steps.explain: `undoDelete` restores the snapshot unchanged. The browser test checks the restored Note equals a with the typed text, `z` included. A drop on the Trash zone calls the same `deleteNote`.

steps.title: pagehide
steps.explain: `pageHidden` ends Editing, so the subscriber saves the Draft text and schedules a Local copy write; `flush` then writes it at once. In the other order, the flush would find nothing scheduled and the text would be lost. This order is not covered by a test.

steps.title: Click a Note and leave it without typing
steps.explain: `draftText` stays `null`, so `endedDraft` returns `null` and the Notes store isn't touched. Typing a change and then typing back to the original text does call `setText`, which returns the same state, so again nobody is notified and nothing is saved.

notes.title: A subscription, not an explicit hand-off
notes.detail: The issue said `deleted(id)` must make the saved text available to `deleteNote`. Instead the Notes store follows the UI store and saves on every Editing ending, so delete needs nothing special: it only reads the Note after `deleted`. Counter-argument: the README says rules spanning both stores are Notes actions, and this one is a subscription that reacts to any UI store `set`. The README now describes it; an ADR could make it official.

notes.title: "Blur" means focus arriving on another Note
notes.detail: The issue lists blur among the endings. It's tested as Tab to the next Note. Switching windows or tabbing to the toolbar doesn't end Editing, as before this PR; the Draft text then stays until Editing ends, or the page is hidden.

notes.title: The Note shows its saved text until something is typed
notes.detail: `draftText` is `null` until the first change, so starting Editing needs no copy of the text, and the UI store never reads the Notes store.

notes.title: Existing tests changed
notes.detail: Two keyboard tests and "keeps text exactly as typed" checked the stored text while still in Editing. They now check the textarea's value, or end Editing first.

notes.title: Glossary
notes.detail: Draft text is defined. Preview keeps "draft" on its avoid list, as the issue says: the two terms are different things.
